title: Sprint commit lanes and automated fallback mapping for hosted API + model catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define and land a clear sprint-level commit lane model for hosted API releases tied to model catalog health signals, and implement automated routing fallback mappings to minimize customer-facing regressions.

Background: As the hosted model catalog grows we need deterministic lanes that map commit windows (canary, staged, fast-follow, full release) to model variants and fallback rules. This ticket unblocks the Q2 cadence by producing a lightweight release contract that ops, eng, and PMs can follow and by delivering the initial automated mapping rules in the control plane so that runtime fallbacks (e.g., lower-latency variant, quantized variant, regional fallback) are enforced automatically when health signals cross thresholds.

Scope:
- Define commit lane definitions, thresholds and required signals (latency p95, token-error-rate, quality regressions from eval hooks).
- Author a short release contract (2 pages) and example checklist for canary -> 50% -> 100% transitions.
- Implement mapping config schema for fallback policies and wire into the routing service (control-plane config only; no runtime kernel changes).
- Add a dashboard panel to Console showing lane status and active fallbacks.
- Automated smoke test that triggers canary rollback when model-quality gating fails.

Out of scope: full runtime circuit-breaker refactor, private/VPC-specific deployment flows (will be tracked separately).

Success criteria:
- Release contract reviewed and signed off by Eng Reliability and Security.
- Mapping config merged and validated against two hosted models in staging.
- Console dashboard visible in staging with lane state and fallback activation events.
- One simulated regression in staging correctly triggers configured fallback and an automated rollback event is logged.
milestones: 2026-03-05: Draft commit lane definitions and thresholds
2026-03-15: Dashboard panel prototype in Console staging
2026-03-22: Integration test & canary smoke tests passing
2026-03-29: Cross-team review (Reliability / Security / DS) and final sign-off
decisions: Use three lanes (canary, staged, general) rather than four to reduce operational complexity
Primary health signals: latency_p95, token_error_rate, eval_quality_delta (thresholds documented in contract)
Fallback preference order: compatible model variant -> quantized variant -> regional replica
risks: False positives from eval_quality_delta could trigger unnecessary rollbacks
Mapping schema might not cover edge cases for multi-model ensemble endpoints
Dashboard noise if thresholds are too tight could reduce on-call signal fidelity
